title: Kernel startup footprint simulator and scheduler advisor
creator: Anika Rao
description: Implement a lightweight simulator that predicts per-request kernel workspace usage, transient allocation peaks, and eviction pressure during startup (prefill) for v2/v3 FlashAttention kernels. The advisor will feed into the scheduler to pick kernels and prefill/decode pacing that minimize OOMs, jitter, and regression risk when switching or probing new kernels.
technical_notes: Goal: reduce incidence of startup OOMs and latency spikes observed during mixed v2/v3 rollouts. The simulator uses a small set of inputs derived from model metadata and recent request telemetry: per-layer head-dim, seq_len distribution, quantization format (fp16/int8), batch size, kv-cache hit ratio estimate, and workspace available on chosen device. It outputs a ranked list of kernel candidates with predicted peak workspace, safe prefill throttle factor, and confidence score. We will integrate with the kernel-prober and prefill-orchestrator to block unsafe kernel activations and automatically apply conservative decode pacing for low-confidence cases. Simulator will run both offline (per-tenant planner) and online in shadow mode (per-request probe) to collect ground truth for calibration.
acceptance_criteria: Simulator prototype exists as a standalone binary/library with documented inputs/outputs
Integration tests validate simulator predictions vs synthetic allocator traces for three representative models (small, medium, long-context)
Scheduler advisor consumes simulator output and reduces observed startup OOM rate by >= 80% on the canary fleet compared to baseline
Telemetry dashboard with predicted vs actual peak workspace and 'confidence' drift available in Console for rollout monitoring
Rollout plan documented with canary gates, rollback thresholds, and automated mitigation (force kernel pin or apply decode throttle)
comments: 2025-02-10 - Anika Rao: Created ticket after postmortem for three canary OOMs during v3 prefills. Initial idea: predictive estimator to avoid speculative kernel swaps.

2025-02-12 - Marcus Chen: Spike prototype implemented. Uses per-layer formula from FA3 workspace model; initial accuracy ~65% on synthetic traces. Found an off-by-one error in kv-size accounting that inflated predictions.

2025-02-14 - QA (Elena Martinez): Ran prototype across small-batch chat workloads. Simulator underestimates by 10-20% for quantized int8 kernels in some long-context layers. Added test vectors and recording hooks.
2025-02-16 - Marcus Chen: Added conservative safety margin for low-confidence cases. Pushed change to PR #2468. CI run shows no regression on unit tests; integration tests running.
2025-02-18 - Observability (R&D): Added telemetry tag 'simulator_confidence' to traces. Initial canary shows predicted/actual correlation 0.88 for fp16, 0.72 for int8.
2025-02-20 - Product (Samir Patel): Requesting a short playbook for on-call describing automated mitigation actions when simulator drift > 25% for > 1h on a tenant.
notes_for_rollout: Phase 1: shadow mode only (no control) for two weeks to collect calibration data. Phase 2: advisory mode where scheduler logs suggested kernel but does not override. Phase 3: canary enforcement on non-critical tenants with automated prefill throttle applied if confidence < 0.7. Gate: OOM rate and 99P latency must remain below baseline +5% during canary. Full rollout contingent on sustained confidence >0.8 for 72h.
implementation_plan: 1) Finalize predictor formulas and incorporate allocator fragmentation model. 2) Add C API wrapper so runtime scheduler can call the simulator cheaply. 3) Instrument runtime to emit predicted vs observed workspace per request. 4) Add console charts and alerting. 5) Run 2-week shadow run, tune safety margins, then progressive enforcement.
risk_assessment: Main risk: simulator underestimates for pathological layer shapes leading to OOMs. Mitigation: conservative margin and 'fail-closed' policy where low-confidence predictions cause scheduler to choose safer kernel (v2) or throttle prefill. Secondary risk: CPU cost of simulator if invoked synchronously; mitigation: run in fast-path C shim and cache recent model predictions per model-version.
